newsitem.title: USA: Texaco brings back most units at Calif. plant.
newsitem.headline: Texaco brings back most units at Calif. plant.

text.p: Texaco Inc said on Tuesday it brought back to full operation all units except a damaged hydrotreater at its 98,000 barrel-per-day refinery in Wilmington, Calif., following an early Monday fire.
"Our refinery is now again operating," a refinery spokeswoman said, adding the fire-damaged number four hydrotreater remains out-of-service and under investigation.
She said plant workers brought back to full operation other units whose production levels had been lowered Monday.
She declined to specify production levels but described the fire's impact as "moderate".
The damaged hydrotreater has a 33,000 bpd capacity and some traders had earlier speculated it could trim the plant's gasoline production by 20,000 bpd.
"We do not expect that we'll experience a shortfall in meeting customers requirements," the plant spokesman said.
Some West Coast product prices rose two cents Monday following news of the fire.
Texaco said early Tuesday it assembled a team to investigate the fire. the group includes experts from inside and outside the company.
